tasks.title: Measurement harness, baselines and the near-first sprite budget (A-1)
tasks.spec:
Enabling work and the critical animation fix. Do this before any change to how players look.

(1) Port the audit scripts from O/audit-scripts/likeness/*.cjs into scripts/qa/, parameterised for the repo root, port 5214 and the output directory O/shots/players/. All of them are isolated: abort every non-localhost request except Google Fonts, open ?ns=inspect&relay=ws://localhost:7777, and use __psInsets. Copy the harness from O/audit-scripts/utui/lib.mjs into scripts/qa/players-lib.mjs. The ported scripts:
- players-sprites.mjs: stale draws by size bucket, hit rate, new drawings/s. Uses ?arcade&auto&seed=spr and ?soccer-lab&auto.
- players-matchperf.mjs: fps, p99 frame interval, frames over 20 ms and rAF cost, at 1x and 4x CDP CPU throttle, at 393x852, 430x932 and 320x568.
- players-lineup.mjs: 12 stars per sport in their own kits and in one shared kit, at 24/40/60 px, plus the card portrait.
- players-strips.mjs: action strips and the pose jump at each hard cut.
- players-cards.mjs: club grid, detail and reveal screenshots, plus a DOM probe for card text sizes, badge contrast and portrait head size.

(2) Capture the BEFORE set as O/shots/players/before-*.png: lineups, cards at 393 and 320, in-game frames, strips. Re-measure every baseline row of plan section 3 on this machine and record it in docs/studio-overhaul/players.md.

(3) New pure module src/game/pixel/sprite-budget.ts with class SpriteBudget: begin(now, frameMs), order(reqs: DrawReq[]), allow(), spent(ms), stale(who). DrawReq is {who, px, must, staleFor, near}.
- Priority: 'must' first (the carrier or handler, the pass target, his nearest defender), then by score px + 24*staleFor.
- Any body of 32 px or more that has been stale for 2 frames is forced.
- The budget is time, not count: 3.0 ms of measured drawBody time, or 2.0 ms when the last frame interval was over 20 ms. Minimum 3 draws, hard cap 14.
- Also in this module: quantPx(raw), with 1 px steps up to 14, 2 px up to 30, 4 px up to 60 and 6 px above. The blit stays 1:1.

(4) In hoops2/render.ts, football2/render.ts and soccer2/render.ts, change only sprite() and the bodies loop in draw():
- Resolve each body's sprite in priority order into a Map<who, Sprite>.
- Then draw them in the existing depth order.
- Replace this.budget = 4|5 with the SpriteBudget.

(5) Pre-warm: in calm frames (pre-snap, before a possession or attack, after a replay), spend up to 2 extra draws a frame on the next gait frames of the 6 nearest bodies; use requestIdleCallback where available.

(6) Raise the SpriteCache caps (NBA 360 to 480, NFL 600 to 800, soccer 700 to 800) only if the measurements show evictions causing misses. Keep CanvasOut recovery and freeCanvas.

Render-only. No sim code is touched. Use thin hunks in the sport-shared render.ts files.

tasks.title: Appearance model, palettes, one build formula, neutral defaults, data pipeline and lazy loader
tasks.spec:
New module src/game/pixel/appearance.ts, following the research doc section 3.1.

Enums:
- HAIR (18): bald, buzz, short, fade, waves, hightop, afro-s, afro-l, twists, locs-s, locs-l, braids, bun, long, mohawk, mullet, curly, receding.
- HAIR_TONE (15): 9 natural, 5 dyed, and 'team'.
- FACIAL (8): none, stubble, mustache, goatee, chinstrap, short, full, long.
- HEAD: none, band-thin, band-wide, wrap, alice, skullcap.
- EYES: none, goggles, mask-clear, visor-clear, visor-dark, visor-tint.
- ARM: none, sleeve, shooter, elbow, wrist, tape, long.
- LEG: none, kneepad, kneesleeve, brace, tights, calf.
- SOCKS: low, crew, high, over-knee.
- ACCENT: white, black, team1, team2, neon, gold, tone.
- BUILD: lean, avg, muscular, stocky, heavy.

Types:
- interface Appearance {v:1, skin?, hair, hairTone, facial, head, headC?, eyes, armL, armR, armC?, legL, legR, legC?, socks, shoe, gloves?, towel?, build?, hand, foot?, motion?, src}
- LookEra = {from, to} & Partial<Appearance>, for per-era overrides.

Palettes:
- SKIN_TONES: the 10 Monk Skin Tone anchors with shadow, highlight and outline, saturation raised 8-15%.
- skinRamp(i) returns [shadow, base, light, outline, rim], with a 1 px rim for tones 7-9.
- NEUTRAL_SKIN = '#a8714f', unchanged for every uncurated player.
- HAIR_TONES: the 15 hexes.
- detailFor(px): the LOD table. headScale(px) = clamp(1 + (32 - px)/64, 1, 1.25).

weightFor(sport, htIn, wt|null, pos) is the one shared build formula: the real weight if known; otherwise soccer uses a BMI by position (GK 23.5, CB 23.6, FB 22.3, DM/CM 22.6, AM/W 22.0, ST 23.2) and NBA/NFL use the SIZE fallbacks.

defaultAppearance(sport, pid, season, pos) is seeded per field with hash(pid + ':field'):
- skin is always neutral
- only neutral hair silhouettes, plausible for the era
- only black, dark brown or brown hair
- facial: none 70%, stubble 15%, short 10%, goatee 5%
- no headband, goggles or sleeves
- socks and shoe colour by era

appearanceFor(sport, pid, season?) resolves curated, then era override, then defaults, and is memoised.

refOf(sport, engineId) parses every id form the engines carry:
- draft 'CHI-1990:pid', using the decade as the season
- UT 'nba:season:1996:pid:CHI'
- 'holo~' and 'evo~a+b~' variants
- live '<sport>:live:<promo>[.f]:<season>:<pid>:<fr>'
- the soccer engine's 'pid:season:fr'
- 'reserve:', 'depth:' and 'squad-', which return null so defaults apply

Loading: loadAppearance(sport) uses import.meta.glob('../../data/appearance/*.json'), one lazy chunk per sport that main-bundle code never imports. Also appearanceReady(sport) and appearanceVersion(). encode/decode helpers are shared with the build script.

Compact built file src/data/appearance/<sport>.json: {v, sport, fields, players: {pid: 'base36 codes[|from-to:codes]...'}, feet?: {L: [], B: []}}.

Human source file src/data/appearance/source/<sport>.looks.json: one object per line with named strings plus name, src and reviewed. App code never imports it.

scripts/build_appearance.ts (vite-node) flags:
- --build
- --check (fails when out of sync)
- --candidates <sport> [n]: ranked by GOAT/Legend tier, best overall and edition count from cards-<sport>.json
- --find <sport> <name>
- --soccer-feet <players.csv.gz> (used in players-3)

New src/game/pixel/looks.ts: matchLook(sport, ref, kit, {pos, ht, wt, gk, pads}) and cardLook(line), each returning the existing Look plus an optional app. Look gains optional app? and pattern?; the legacy hair and beard fields are kept.

Add 2-3 fixture entries per sport only. Real curation is players-3. No drawing changes in this task.

tasks.title: Transitions and grounded locomotion (A-2 blends, contact lock; A-5 foot anchoring, gait rates, frame rates, facings)
tasks.spec:
(1) New src/game/pixel/blend.ts:
- blendJoints(a, b, t): bone-direction slerp from the pelvis out, rebuilt with the target body's bone lengths. Hand-keyed poses go through rig.joints() first.
- A transition memo {fromKey, fromJoints, start, dur}.
- When the animation's identity (clip or pose family) changes, blend for 100 ms (6 frames at 60 Hz), quantised to 3 steps. The sprite key becomes key + '~' + fromKey + step.
- Contact lock: a blend never spans an event frame (release, catch, contact, plant, impact); shorten it so the warped event lands on the engine frame.
- Contact reactions (falls, stumbles, posterized) cut in at 0 frames.
- A player-initiated action changes the drawn picture on its first frame.
- Gait entry is phase-matched from the stepL/stepR beats.

(2) New src/game/pixel/locomotion.ts, pure and shared by the three gait() functions:
- pickGait(speed, clipSpeeds) chooses walk, jog, run or sprint, with the rate clamped to 0.8-1.25x; outside that range it switches clip.
- Remove the dead bands: NBA run below 2.5 ft/s showing ready; the static NBA defend pose at 1-3 ft/s (use shuffle or backpedal at matched rates); soccer ready while drifting 0.15-1 m/s (use walk); the NBA backpedal rate cap.
- Add a new 'walk' clip from a CMU walking trial via scripts/build_mocap.py --inspect. Use MOCAP_CACHE=<worktree>/.cache/mocap/bvh, which is git-ignored, seeded from the main checkout's cache. Regenerate src/data/mocap/walk.json and index.json.
- Stance-foot anchoring (R4): plantedFoot(clip, frame) from beats and foot heights. The renderer offsets the sprite so the planted toe stays on its screen anchor. The sim position leads, through a damper of at most 0.5x the gait's own displacement per frame; it re-anchors at each strike and decays to 0 when airborne. The ball and hand take the same offset.
- Rates: step 1 (30 fps) for the handler or carrier, his marker and any sprite of 40 px or more; step 2 for the rest; idles at step 2 for 32 px and up; NFL and soccer sprites under 22 px go from step 3 or more to step 2 when the budget allows.
- turnToward(memo, target, dt) for all three sports: a 90-degree turn takes 80-120 ms; spins, dives and falls are exempt. Use 16 facings from 18 px when the budget allows.
- NFL QB drop: in the drop phase while moving, play backpedal at a matched rate facing downfield, instead of the ready idle (which skates 6.5 yd).

(3) Thin hooks in animOf, gait, sprite() and the sprite x/y in each render.ts bodies loop.

The plan is at /home/user/ps-s-players/docs/studio-overhaul/players-plan.md. It was committed as 3790d50 ('Claude: add the players team build plan for the studio overhaul'), with only that file staged and the required trailer, and pushed to origin claude/studio-players as a new branch.

**Order and dependencies.** players-1 (A-1, the critical bug, plus the measurement harness and BEFORE captures) comes first because it is independent of likeness and must capture baselines before anything changes how players look. Then 2 (model) → 3 (data) → 4 (drawing and engine wiring) → 5 (transitions and foot planting), all P0. The P1 card tasks 6 and 7 come before the P1 animation tasks 8 and 9; players-10 is the release gate. Task 4 needs 2 (and 3 for the star screenshots); 5 needs 1; 6 needs 4's head.ts; 7 needs 6; 8 needs 5; 9 needs 8 and 2.

**Size.** Tasks 4, 8 and 9 are the largest, about 3-4 hours each. Each has explicit stretch items with a rule to defer them rather than drop them: L-6 kit patterns in 4, WalkoutFigure in 9.

**Protocol.** No bump is planned. Every task is render-only, and render-only.test.ts proves it with an import-graph check plus seeded runs with and without appearance loaded.

**Lane.**
- Thin hunks only in the player-drawing parts of the three render.ts files; all new logic goes in new src/game/pixel/* modules to avoid conflicts with the sport teams' camera and HUD work.

- 39 CMU trials are already cached at /home/user/perfect-season/.cache/mocap/bvh; seed a worktree MOCAP_CACHE from it.

I revised the plan, committed it as 835fd70 and pushed it to claude/studio-players. File: /home/user/ps-s-players/docs/studio-overhaul/players-plan.md.

Section 9 of the plan answers every critique point: 25 missing items, 17 restructures, 18 risks and 28 targets. Each row is marked accepted, partial or rejected, with the reason.

The critique's splits plus its added scope come to about 14 sessions of work, against a cap of 10 tasks. I kept 10 tasks this way:
- **Contracts written now.** Section 6 holds the action contract, reserved act names, the ownership splits, the HUD/portrait/walkout/impactOf/readiness contracts and the reports, so players-1 only publishes them.
- **Selection code moved first.** players-2 moves lookFor/animOf/gait/poseOf into players-owned select-*.ts modules. Later tasks then work in our own files, and the window for render.ts conflicts shrinks.
- **Tiers.** The large tasks have ordered must and stretch tiers, with a carry-over rule: unfinished must items open the next task, and unreached stretch items go to the named phase-2 list.

**Splits accepted and rejected:**
- Accepted: players-1 split into harness and render core; owner-value reorder (card faces at #3, busts at #6, both before the animation core).
- Partial: the drawing split (extraction moved to players-2 instead); the actions split (impact moved to players-8).
- Rejected as separate tasks because of the cap: curation into three tasks. Mitigation: three per-sport commits each ending in a contact sheet, 30 seed rows per sport in players-4, and separate must and target lines.
- Post-merge verification is a lead step using players-verify.mjs, because the merged tree only exists after the lead merges.

**Critique items rejected on substance:** the random 10% lefty prior, the random 75/20/5 soccer foot and the 'other natural 5%' hair tone (each lowers expected accuracy and is a salient false cue), and the '99+' face cap (it would hide the Spotlight/GOAT chase; we show true values in condensed numerals).

**Skin tone:** it comes only from a cited public Commons photo, picked against the 10 swatches, otherwise neutral. If Commons/Wikidata are unreachable, skin stays neutral and is flagged 'skin pending' for the owner device check.

**Lead rulings requested:**
- card-face.ts treated as read-only and moved to packs
- camera, floor and stands code in persp/court/field/pitch going to the sport teams (players keeps one-line crowd.ts calls)
- the soccer on-demand regex diff for shell
- assigning the nba/nfl name-tag calls and the NBA-26 roster intro
- a decision on the brand-like 2K badge names shown in CardDetail (abilityName/ABILITY_HELP, Heat Check), which nba/packs own

**Outside our lane:** an ~8-line juice.ts hunk, docs/CREDITS.md, scripts/build_mocap.py, a read-only copy of the main checkout's mocap cache, and possibly one-line crowd calls.

**Unverified assumptions:**
- The plan assumes nba/nfl/soccer register their new acts through the intake before players-9; later acts get the family fallback.
- The impactOf call-site wiring and the pixelReady loading-gate line belong to other teams and only count as done when seen at merge.
